title: What If You Sold Every Minecraft Copy Yourself?
description:
Minecraft sold over 400 million copies. Now try selling them one by one.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Minecraft: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minecraft
- Wikipedia: Mojang Studios: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojang_Studios
- Wikipedia: Markus Persson: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_Persson

Wikipedia (Minecraft): the best-selling video game of all time, over 400 million copies sold; it passed one million purchases less than a month into its beta in early 2011, with no publisher and no ads beyond word of mouth. Wikipedia (Mojang Studios / Markus Persson): Microsoft agreed to buy Mojang for $2.5 billion in September 2014. Our math: 400 million seconds = about 12.7 years. Not financial advice.

#shorts #minecraft #gaming #howtheymakemoney
loop: So next time you place a block, remember:
cta: Survival or creative? Comment your pick.

scenes.narration: Minecraft sold over 400 million copies. Now try selling them one by one.
One sale every second? That still takes 12.7 years.
It started tiny, though. Just word of mouth, no ads. Then a million sales.
Then Microsoft bought its maker for 2.5 billion dollars.

problems: The character model has no face/features, which looks low-effort and off-putting.
The number '$2.1 BILLION' appears on screen while the narration says '2.5 billion dollars', creating a direct contradiction.
The text '108 MILLION' appears on screen at the start, but the narration says '400 million'.
The character's movement and the environment look generic and cheap, failing to capture the 'Minecraft' aesthetic.
The final frame repeats the title text, which is redundant and feels like a filler ending.
eyes.best_fix: Align all on-screen text and numbers with the narration and replace the faceless character model with a more expressive or stylized avatar that fits the Minecraft theme.
